claim: Pathogenic variants in subunits of RNA polymerase (Pol) III cause a spectrum of Polr3-related neurodegenerative diseases including 4H leukodystrophy.
source: Pathogenic variants in subunits of RNA polymerase (Pol) III cause a spectrum of Polr3-related neurodegenerative diseases including 4H leukodystrophy.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature (Lata et al., 2021; Watt et al., 2023) as indicated in the full text.

claim: Disease onset occurs from infancy to early adulthood and is associated with a variable range and severity of neurological and non-neurological features.
source: Disease onset occurs from infancy to early adulthood and is associated with a variable range and severity of neurological and non-neurological features.
evidence: This is a general characterization of Polr3-related disease based on established clinical knowledge.

claim: The molecular basis of Polr3-related disease pathogenesis is unknown.
source: The molecular basis of Polr3-related disease pathogenesis is unknown.
evidence: This statement reflects the gap in knowledge that motivates the study.

claim: Polr3a mutant mice exhibit behavioral deficits, cerebral pathology and exocrine pancreatic atrophy.
source: Polr3a mutant mice exhibit behavioral deficits, cerebral pathology and exocrine pancreatic atrophy.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including behavioral testing, histology, and imaging.

claim: Transcriptome and immunohistochemistry analyses of cerebra during disease progression show a reduction in most Pol III transcripts, induction of innate immune and integrated stress responses and cell-type-specific gene expression changes reflecting neuron and oligodendrocyte loss and microglial activation.
source: Transcriptome and immunohistochemistry analyses of cerebra during disease progression show a reduction in most Pol III transcripts, induction of innate immune and integrated stress responses and cell-type-specific gene expression changes reflecting neuron and oligodendrocyte loss and microglial activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data, RT-qPCR, Northern blotting, and immunohistochemistry presented in the manuscript.

claim: Earlier in the disease when integrated stress and innate immune responses are minimally induced, mature tRNA sequencing revealed a global reduction in tRNA levels and an altered tRNA profile but no changes in other Pol III transcripts.
source: Earlier in the disease when integrated stress and innate immune responses are minimally induced, mature tRNA sequencing revealed a global reduction in tRNA levels and an altered tRNA profile but no changes in other Pol III transcripts.
evidence: This claim is supported by QuantM-tRNA-seq data and RT-qPCR analysis at P42 timepoint.

claim: Changes in the size and/or composition of the tRNA pool have a causal role in disease initiation.
source: Thus, changes in the size and/or composition of the tRNA pool have a causal role in disease initiation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the temporal sequence of molecular changes observed in the study.

claim: Different tissue- and brain region-specific sensitivities to a defect in Pol III transcription exist.
source: Our findings reveal different tissue- and brain region-specific sensitivities to a defect in Pol III transcription.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative analysis of multiple tissues and brain regions showing differential responses to the Polr3a mutation.

claim: Patients with Polr3-related leukodystrophy typically present in early childhood with motor deficits and developmental delay.
source: Patients with Polr3-related leukodystrophy typically present in early childhood with motor deficits and developmental delay.
evidence: This is a clinical characterization based on literature.

claim: The disease is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
source: The disease is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner, is progressive and exhibits wide ranging phenotypic severity from premature death during infancy to mild forms that have been diagnosed in adults (Watt et al., 2023).
evidence: This is established genetic knowledge about Polr3-related disease supported by citation.

claim: Initial findings of hypomyelination are not universal as some patients have normal or near normal myelination but distinct MRI and neuropathological changes that suggest a largely neuronal phenotype.
source: Notably, initial findings of hypomyelination, suggesting oligodendrocyte involvement, are not universal as some patients have normal or near normal myelination but distinct MRI and neuropathological changes that suggest a largely neuronal phenotype (Perrier et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to clinical literature.

claim: It is unclear why mutations in Pol III result in phenotypes primarily of the central nervous system.
source: It is also unclear why mutations in Pol III, a ubiquitously-expressed, essential enzyme responsible for the synthesis of critical non-coding RNAs central to protein synthesis, pre-mRNA splicing, secretion and other processes, result in phenotypes primarily of the central nervous system.
evidence: This statement identifies a key question motivating the research.

claim: Experiments with patient-derived fibroblasts and CRISPR-Cas9 engineered cell lines show that precursor tRNA levels are generally lower.
source: Collectively, experiments with patient-derived fibroblasts and CRISPR-Cas9 engineered cell lines show that precursor tRNA levels are generally lower but only one of four mature tRNAs tested in two different studies were reduced, suggesting that high tRNA stability can compensate for defects in synthesis (Choquet et al., 2019; Dorboz et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: 7SL RNA levels were uniformly lower in agreement with a separate analysis of Pol III-derived transcripts in patient blood.
source: 7SL RNA levels were uniformly lower in agreement with a separate analysis of Pol III-derived transcripts in patient blood (Azmanov et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Brain-specific expression of pathogenic Polr3a mutations (W671R/G672E) in the mouse Olig2 lineage resulted in impaired growth and developmental delay, deficits in cognitive, sensory, and fine sensorimotor function, and hypomyelination in multiple regions of the cerebrum and spinal cord.
source: In previous work we showed that brain-specific expression of pathogenic Polr3a mutations (W671R/G672E) in the mouse Olig2 lineage resulted in impaired growth and developmental delay, deficits in cognitive, sensory, and fine sensorimotor function, and hypomyelination in multiple regions of the cerebrum and spinal cord (Merheb et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Recombination frequencies were ~60% in liver, ∼70% in cerebrum, ∼80% in cerebellum and kidney and ~90% in heart.
source: Recombination frequencies determined by flow cytometry or fluorescence microscopy using a dual tdTomato-EGFP reporter were ~60% in liver, ∼70% in cerebrum, ∼80% in cerebellum and kidney and ~90% in heart (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry and microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Polr3a-tamKI mice have significantly lower body weights than tamoxifen-injected WT controls.
source: Tamoxifen-induced knockin mice (denoted as Polr3a-tamKI mice) have significantly lower body weights than tamoxifen-injected WT controls.
evidence: This claim is supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Body weight differences appear in both sexes at P34 and become progressively larger as Polr3a-tamKI mice lose weight while the control mice gain weight over time.
source: Body weight differences appear in both sexes at P34 and become progressively larger as Polr3a-tamKI mice lose weight while the control mice gain weight over time (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by longitudinal body weight data in Figure 1C.

claim: A growth defect was reported previously for Polr3a-Olig2KI mice.
source: Notably, a growth defect was reported previously for Polr3a-Olig2KI mice (formerly Polr3a-cKI mice, Merheb et al., 2021), consistent with the reduced stature of many patients with Pol III-related leukodystrophy (Watt et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Polr3a-Olig2KI mice gain weight, albeit more slowly than controls, from adolescence to adulthood despite their smaller size.
source: However, in contrast to the current model, Polr3a-Olig2KI mice gain weight, albeit more slowly than controls, from adolescence to adulthood despite their smaller size (Merheb et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The loss of body weight in Polr3a-tamKI mice demonstrates a more severe failure to thrive phenotype, in line with the widespread expression of the Polr3a mutation.
source: Thus, the loss of body weight in Polr3a-tamKI mice demonstrates a more severe failure to thrive phenotype, in line with the widespread expression of the Polr3a mutation.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of the current model with the previous Olig2-specific model.

claim: LFB staining of coronal sections of the cerebrum revealed impaired myelin deposition in Polr3a-tamKI cortex, hippocampus and thalamus with qualitatively greater differences in the cortex at P90.
source: LFB staining of coronal sections of the cerebrum revealed impaired myelin deposition in Polr3a-tamKI cortex, hippocampus and thalamus with qualitatively greater differences in the cortex at P90 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by LFB staining images in Figure 1E.

claim: LFB- and Nissl-stained sagittal sections of the cerebellum showed no differences in myelin or granular layer neurons, respectively, and no difference in Purkinje cell density.
source: In contrast, LFB- and Nissl-stained sagittal sections of the cerebellum showed no differences in myelin or granular layer neurons, respectively, and no difference in Purkinje cell density (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: The absence of a myelination defect in the cerebellum was previously noted in Polr3a-Olig2KI mice.
source: The absence of a myelination defect in the cerebellum was previously noted in Polr3a-Olig2KI mice (Merheb et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Non-CNS tissues (>20 examined) were histologically normal except for the pancreas.
source: Non-CNS tissues (>20 examined) were histologically normal except for the pancreas.
evidence: This claim is based on histopathological examination of multiple tissues.

claim: Polr3a-tamKI mice exhibit pronounced and severe exocrine pancreatic atrophy at P42 and P90, respectively.
source: Polr3a-tamKI mice exhibit pronounced and severe exocrine pancreatic atrophy at P42 and P90, respectively (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by H&E staining of pancreatic tissue in Figure 1F.

claim: Exocrine pancreatic atrophy is characterized by insufficient production of digestive enzymes.
source: This condition is characterized by insufficient production of digestive enzymes (Kleeff et al., 2017) and correlates with the lower body weight of Polr3a-tamKI mice, the marked reduction in subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue at P90, and the poor health of the mice at this age.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the literature and correlation with observed phenotypes.

claim: Body fat as a percentage of total body weight was comparable to WT at P42.
source: In contrast to the paucity of body fat at P90, echoMRI measurements at P42 showed that body fat as a percentage of total body weight was comparable to WT (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by echoMRI data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Blood glucose concentrations increased upon feeding and were not significantly different between Polr3a-tamKI and WT mice in either the fasted or the refed state.
source: Blood glucose concentrations increased upon feeding, as expected, and were not significantly different between Polr3a-tamKI and WT mice in either the fasted or the refed state (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by blood glucose measurements in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: A glucose tolerance test showed comparable responses between Polr3a-tamKI and WT mice.
source: Similarly, a glucose tolerance test showed comparable responses (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by glucose tolerance test data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Endocrine pancreatic functions controlling glucose homeostasis are not significantly impaired at P42 by the Polr3a mutation.
source: These data suggest that endocrine pancreatic functions controlling glucose homeostasis are not significantly impaired at P42 by the Polr3a mutation.
evidence: This is an inference based on glucose homeostasis measurements.

claim: No differences were observed in anxiety-like behavior.
source: No differences were observed in anxiety-like behavior, which was assessed using metrics that measure the natural tendency of mice to avoid open spaces (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: Overall locomotor activity was decreased in Polr3a-tamKI mice as indicated by the reduced track length at P42, P49, P56, and P63.
source: However, overall locomotor activity was decreased in Polr3a-tamKI mice as indicated by the reduced track length at P42, P49, P56, and P63 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral tracking data in Figure 2A.

claim: Polr3a-tamKI mice spent less time running and more time standing still at all time points compared to WT mice.
source: Polr3a-tamKI mice also spent less time running and more time standing still at all time points compared to WT mice, consistent with a locomotor deficit (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data in Figure 2B and C.

claim: Polr3a-tamKI mice spend less time assessing risk at all time points.
source: The sum of these behaviors shows that Polr3a-tamKI mice spend less time assessing risk at all time points (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data in Figure 2D.

claim: Polr3a-tamKI mice showed lower levels of exploration compared to WT mice at all timepoints although the data did not reach significance at P49.
source: When all three rearing metrics were combined, Polr3a-tamKI mice showed lower levels of exploration compared to WT mice at all timepoints although the data did not reach significance at P49 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data in Figure 2E.

claim: The Polr3a-tamKI mice spent less time grooming their legs and back compared to WT mice starting at P49 and progressing to P63.
source: The Polr3a-tamKI mice spent less time grooming their legs and back compared to WT mice starting at P49 and progressing to P63.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1J, K.

claim: Head grooming was reduced at P63.
source: Head grooming was also reduced at P63.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1J.

claim: The findings reveal behavioral phenotypes in Polr3a-tamKI mice at the earliest time point in the study, two weeks after introduction of the mutation, consistent with neurobehavioral deficits.
source: In summary, the findings reveal behavioral phenotypes in Polr3a-tamKI mice at the earliest time point in the study, two weeks after introduction of the mutation, consistent with neurobehavioral deficits (Brodkin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on the behavioral data and supported by citation.

claim: None of the affected behaviors were apparent in Polr3a-Olig2KI mice.
source: As none of the affected behaviors were apparent in Polr3a-Olig2KI mice (Merheb et al., 2021), the data further demonstrate that the mutation has a more severe impact on animal behavior when its expression is induced postnatally in many cell types than when it is induced during embryonic development only in the Olig2 lineage.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work and comparison with current findings.

claim: The levels of four precursor tRNAs were reduced ~threefold in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
source: The levels of four precursor tRNAs, determined either by northern blotting for intron sequences or by RT-qPCR with precursor-specific primers, were reduced ~threefold in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Northern blotting and RT-qPCR data in Figure 3A–C.

claim: Northern blotting of four mature tRNAs showed that all were lower in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra with two of them reduced to ~60% of the WT.
source: Nonetheless, Northern blotting of four mature tRNAs showed that all were lower in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra with two of them reduced to ~60% of the WT (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Northern blotting data in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Transcripts from genes with a tRNA-like Type II promoter showed a decrease in abundance to between 45% and 60% of the WT level.
source: Transcripts from genes with a tRNA-like Type II promoter (e.g. 7SL, BC1 and Mvg1, aka Vault RNA) showed a decrease in abundance to between 45% and 60% of the WT level (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3C.

claim: Transcripts from genes with a Type III promoter were variably decreased: Rpph1 and 7SK RNAs were decreased to 70% and 56%, respectively, while U6, U6atac and Rmrp RNAs were unaffected.
source: Transcripts from genes with a Type III promoter (e.g. U6, Rmrp, Rpph1, and 7SK RNAs), were variably decreased: Rpph1 and 7SK RNAs were decreased to 70% and 56%, respectively, while U6, U6atac and Rmrp RNAs were unaffected.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3C.

claim: The level of 5S rRNA was elevated.
source: The level of 5S rRNA, the only RNA produced using a Type I promoter, was elevated (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3C.

claim: A two to sixfold upregulation was measured for seven ATF4-regulated ISR target genes, two others were induced at lower levels and one was unaffected.
source: A two to sixfold upregulation was measured for seven of these genes, two others were induced at lower levels and one was unaffected (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3D.

claim: These results point to altered translation in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
source: These results point to altered translation in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
evidence: This is an inference based on ISR gene expression data.

claim: Differentially expressed (DE) genes (p adj. <0.05, log2FoldChange >|0.58|) were biased towards upregulation; 83% of DE genes were increased in the Polr3a mutant.
source: Differentially expressed (DE) genes (p adj. <0.05, log2FoldChange >|0.58|) were biased towards upregulation; 83% of DE genes were increased in the Polr3a mutant (Figure 3E, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data in Figure 3E and Supplementary file 1.

claim: 192 ATF4-dependent ISR genes were upregulated in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
source: We compared our DE genes with a list of 774 ISR genes that show ATF4-dependent induction following tunicamycin treatment of mouse embryo fibroblasts (Torrence et al., 2021) and found 192 genes upregulated in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and comparison with published ISR gene lists.

claim: Expression of the transcription factor ATF6 and its canonical ERAD targets were not affected suggesting that ISR induction in the Polr3a mutant does not involve an ER stress-mediated Unfolded Protein Response.
source: Interestingly, expression of the transcription factor ATF6 and its canonical ERAD targets (Pdia4, Pdia6, Edem1, Grp78 aka Hspa5, Grp94 aka Hsp90b1, Xbp1, and Canx) were not affected suggesting that ISR induction in the Polr3a mutant does not involve an ER stress-mediated Unfolded Protein Response (UPR, Supplementary file 1; Hillary and FitzGerald, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and citation to the literature.

claim: The relative levels of inactive unspliced and active spliced forms of Xbp1 were unchanged.
source: This was confirmed by showing that the relative levels of inactive unspliced and active spliced forms of Xbp1, a critical transcription factor for the UPR, were unchanged (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Metascape pathway enrichment of upregulated DE genes identified activation of the immune system and related processes as major functional categories.
source: Metascape pathway enrichment of upregulated DE genes identified activation of the immune system and related processes as major functional categories (Figure 3F, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by pathway enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: All mitochondrially encoded transcripts were down-regulated in the Polr3a mutant.
source: All mitochondrially encoded transcripts were also down-regulated in the Polr3a mutant (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data in Figure 3E.

claim: qPCR analysis showed that the ratio of two mitochondrial genes to a nuclear gene was substantially reduced in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
source: Indeed, qPCR analysis showed that the ratio of two mitochondrial genes (Mt-Rnr2 and Mt-Nd1) to a nuclear gene (Hk2) was substantially reduced in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The loss of mitochondrial genomes underlies the reduction in mitochondrially encoded RNA detected by RNAseq.
source: Thus, the loss of mitochondrial genomes underlies the reduction in mitochondrially encoded RNA detected by RNAseq.
evidence: This is an inference based on qPCR and RNA-seq data.

claim: Hmgcr and Sqle were among numerous sterol biosynthetic genes down-regulated in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
source: Hmgcr and Sqle were among numerous sterol biosynthetic genes down-regulated in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and Supplementary file 1.

claim: These enzymes function in rate-limiting steps in de novo cholesterol synthesis, suggesting dysfunctional cholesterol production.
source: These enzymes function in rate-limiting steps in de novo cholesterol synthesis, suggesting dysfunctional cholesterol production.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known functions of these enzymes and their reduced expression.

claim: Impairment of cholesterol biosynthesis in either astrocytes or oligodendrocytes can result in cognitive and behavioral phenotypes.
source: Impairment of cholesterol biosynthesis in either cell type can result in cognitive and behavioral phenotypes (Li et al., 2022) and thus may contribute to the behavioral defects noted in Polr3a-tamKI mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the literature and used to infer potential mechanisms.

claim: Twenty-one percent of Polr3a-tamKI DE genes could be assigned to one of five cell types (OLs, neurons, astrocytes, microglia and endothelial cells) with microglia and neurons constituting the bulk of the cell-type-specific genes.
source: Twenty-one percent of Polr3a-tamKI DE genes (p-adj <0.05) could be assigned to one of these five cell types with microglia and neurons constituting the bulk of the cell-type-specific genes (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of RNA-seq data against cell-type-specific gene signatures.

claim: OL and neuronal gene expression was predominantly down-regulated suggesting a reduction in these cell populations while microglia were predominantly elevated.
source: OL and neuronal gene expression was predominantly down-regulated suggesting a reduction in these cell populations while microglia were predominantly elevated (Figure 4A–C, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and cell-type-specific gene expression analysis in Figure 4A–C.

claim: Immunohistochemistry confirmed that changes in cell type gene expression signatures correlated with changes in cell-specific protein markers.
source: Immunohistochemistry confirmed that these changes in cell type gene expression signatures correlated with changes in cell-specific protein markers (Figure 4D–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 4D–H.

claim: The mean fluorescence intensity of myelin basic protein (MBP) staining in the corpus callosum of adult Polr3a-tamKI mice was not significantly diminished relative to WT.
source: Accordingly, the mean fluorescence intensity of myelin basic protein (MBP) staining in the corpus callosum of adult Polr3a-tamKI mice was not significantly diminished relative to WT.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence quantification in Figure 4E.

claim: The density of MBP staining was reduced as was the number of OLs staining positive with the CC1 antibody.
source: However, the density of MBP staining was reduced as was the number of OLs staining positive with the CC1 antibody (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4D and E.

claim: The mean fluorescence intensity of NeuN staining and the number of NeuN positive neuronal nuclei was lower in Polr3a-tamKI mice.
source: In the cerebral cortex, the mean fluorescence intensity of NeuN staining and the number of NeuN positive neuronal nuclei was lower in Polr3a-tamKI mice (Figure 4F) consistent with the decrease in neuron-specific gene expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4F.

claim: Reactive microglia were observed in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra, as evidenced by the increased cell density and altered morphology of Iba1-stained cells in the cortex and particularly in the striatum.
source: Additionally, we observed reactive microglia in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra, as evidenced by the increased cell density and altered morphology (enlarged cell bodies and shorter, thicker processes) of Iba1-stained cells in the cortex and particularly in the striatum (Figure 4G and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4G and H.

claim: Behavioral deficits, induction of the ISR, loss of mitochondrial genomes, an elevated immune response and neurodegeneration are causally linked to the loss of Pol III transcription in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
source: Together, these data indicate that behavioral deficits, induction of the ISR, loss of mitochondrial genomes, an elevated immune response and neurodegeneration are causally linked to the loss of Pol III transcription in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective findings from multiple experiments.

claim: The levels of three precursor tRNAs in the cerebellum, heart, kidney were reduced ~threefold, comparable to the changes seen in cerebra.
source: The levels of three precursor tRNAs in the cerebellum, heart, kidney were reduced ~threefold, comparable to the changes seen in cerebra (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by Northern blotting and RT-qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In the liver, only one of the three precursor tRNAs was reduced.
source: However, in the liver, where the efficiency of CAGGCre-ER recombination is lower (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C; Hayashi and McMahon, 2002), only one of the three precursor tRNAs was reduced (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by Northern blotting and RT-qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The levels of two mature tRNAs were variably affected, being unchanged in liver and cerebella, trending lower in heart and reduced in kidney to ~70% of WT.
source: The levels of two mature tRNAs were variably affected, being unchanged in liver and cerebella, trending lower in heart and reduced in kidney to ~70% of WT (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by Northern blotting data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Tissues other than cerebra showed few changes among other Pol III transcripts: 7SL and Rmrp RNA levels were reduced in cerebella but otherwise no reductions were detected.
source: Among other Pol III transcripts, tissues other than cerebra showed few changes: 7SL and Rmrp RNA levels were reduced in cerebella but otherwise no reductions were detected (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: There was little indication of an ISR response in the tested tissues other than cerebra.
source: Similarly, there was little indication of an ISR response in the tested tissues other than cerebra (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The diminished activity of Pol III in tissues other than cerebra is above the threshold necessary for ISR induction.
source: These data imply that the diminished activity of Pol III in these tissues is above the threshold necessary for ISR induction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of ISR induction in multiple tissues despite reduced Pol III activity.

claim: Polr3a-tamKI pre-tRNA levels were reduced ~threefold at P42.
source: Similar to the P75 time point, Polr3a-tamKI pre-tRNA levels were reduced ~threefold and three out of four mature tRNAs were reduced to ~60% of the WT level (compare Figure 5A–C with Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Northern blotting and RT-qPCR data in Figure 5A–C.

claim: Three out of four mature tRNAs were reduced to ~60% of the WT level at P42.
source: Similar to the P75 time point, Polr3a-tamKI pre-tRNA levels were reduced ~threefold and three out of four mature tRNAs were reduced to ~60% of the WT level (compare Figure 5A–C with Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Northern blotting data in Figure 5A and B.

claim: No Pol III transcripts other than tRNAs were decreased at P42.
source: No Pol III transcripts other than tRNAs were decreased at P42 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 5C.

claim: Decreased production of precursor and mature tRNA is the earliest detectable Pol III defect in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
source: Thus, decreased production of precursor and mature tRNA is the earliest detectable Pol III defect in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
evidence: This is an inference based on temporal analysis of Pol III transcripts.

claim: Fewer ATF4-regulated ISR genes were induced in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra at P42 and the response was less robust than at P75.
source: Analysis of the ATF4-regulated ISR gene panel revealed that fewer genes were induced in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra at P42 and the response was less robust than at P75 (compare Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data comparing P42 and P75 timepoints.

claim: Sesn2, Mthfd2, Chac1, Ald1l2, and Asns were up-regulated twofold or less indicating partial activation of the ISR at P42.
source: Sesn2, Mthfd2, Chac1, Ald1l2, and Asns were up-regulated twofold or less indicating partial activation of the ISR.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Bulk RNAseq showed fewer significant DE genes at P42 (181 genes) with 68% up-regulated and minimal overlap with the P75 DE gene set.
source: Bulk RNAseq showed fewer significant DE genes at P42 (181 genes) with 68% up-regulated and minimal overlap with the P75 DE gene set (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data in Figure 5D and Supplementary file 3.

claim: The expression of mitochondrially-encoded genes was unaffected at P42, as was mitochondrial genome content.
source: Additionally, the expression of mitochondrially-encoded genes was unaffected at P42, as was mitochondrial genome content (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq and qPCR data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Iba1-staining did not reveal any increase in the density of microglia in the cerebral cortex or the striatum at P42.
source: Consistent with these data at P42 and in contrast to the findings at P75, Iba1-staining did not reveal any increase in the density of microglia in the cerebral cortex or the striatum (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F, G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F, G.

claim: There is a progression of stress and immune response programs with time in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
source: Together these data indicate a progression of stress and immune response programs with time in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of P42 and P75 timepoints.

claim: Total nuclear-encoded tRNA reads were significantly lower in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra suggesting an ~25% reduction in total tRNA abundance.
source: Total nuclear-encoded tRNA reads normalized with either or both standards were similar and significantly lower in Polr3a-tamKI cerebra suggesting an ~25% reduction in total tRNA abundance (Figure 6A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This claim is supported by QuantM-tRNA-seq data in Figure 6A.

claim: The majority of tRNA isodecoders (58%, 108/187 tRNAs with p-adj <0.05) were significantly lower in the Polr3a mutant.
source: Differential expression (DE) analysis indicated that the majority of tRNA isodecoders (i.e. tRNAs that share the same anticodon but have different body sequences) were significantly lower in the Polr3a mutant (58%, 108/187 tRNAs with p-adj <0.05, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by differential expression analysis of tRNA-seq data.

claim: The three tRNAiMet isodecoders were less dramatically affected, reduced to 86–88% of the WT level.
source: Compared to most elongator tRNAs, the three tRNAiMet isodecoders were less dramatically affected, reduced to 86–88% of the WT level.
evidence: This claim is supported by tRNA-seq data in Figure 6B.

claim: The level of n-TRtct5 was unchanged in the Polr3a mutant.
source: The level of n-TRtct5 (aka tRNA-Arg-TCT-4–1) an abundant neuron-enriched tRNA that is mutated in the C57BL/6 J background and causes synthetic phenotypes when combined with ribosome rescue factor mutants (Ishimura et al., 2014; Terrey et al., 2020), was unchanged in the Polr3a mutant.
evidence: This claim is supported by tRNA-seq data in Figure 6B.

claim: The cerebral phenotypes of Polr3a-tamKI mice are unlikely to result from synthetic effects of the n-TRtct5 and Polr3a mutations.
source: Thus, the cerebral phenotypes of Polr3a-tamKI mice are unlikely to result from synthetic effects of the n-TRtct5 and Polr3a mutations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the unchanged level of n-TRtct5.

claim: All tRNA decoders were reduced in the Polr3a mutant, and for 30 decoders (60%), the reductions were significant.
source: Indeed, when tRNA read counts were combined into their respective decoder (i.e. anticodon) groups, all decoders were reduced in the Polr3a mutant, and for 30 decoders (60%), the reductions were significant (Figure 6F, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by tRNA-seq data in Figure 6F.

claim: tRNAVal(AAC) and tRNATyr(GTA) were proportionally less abundant than tRNAHis(GTG), and seven other tRNAs, respectively.
source: For example, tRNAVal(AAC) and tRNATyr(GTA) were proportionally less abundant than tRNAHis(GTG), and seven other tRNAs, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by tRNA profile analysis in Figure 6E.

claim: The most severely affected decoders were tRNAVal(AAC) (to 48% of the WT level), tRNATyr(GTA) (to 50%), tRNASup(TCA) (to 53%), tRNASer(AGA) (to 63%) and tRNAGln(CTG) (to 64%).
source: The most severely affected decoders were tRNAVal(AAC) (to 48% of the WT level), tRNATyr(GTA) (to 50%), tRNASup(TCA) (to 53%), tRNASer(AGA) (to 63%) and tRNAGln(CTG) (to 64%).
evidence: This claim is supported by tRNA-seq data in Figure 6F.

claim: The decrease in tRNA decoders is likely to negatively affect the tRNA decoding potential at the earliest stage of disease pathogenesis.
source: These findings suggest that the decrease in tRNA decoders is likely to negatively affect the tRNA decoding potential at the earliest stage of disease pathogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed changes in tRNA levels and their known roles in translation.

claim: Total tRNA abundance was reduced in cerebella by ~23% in the Polr3a mutant.
source: QuantM-tRNA-seq indicated that total tRNA abundance was reduced in cerebella by ~23% in the Polr3a mutant (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), similar to cerebra, and the expression of tRNA isodecoders was broadly decreased (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: This claim is supported by tRNA-seq data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Fewer tRNAs (30 vs 108) and fewer tRNA decoders (11 vs 30) achieved statistical significance in Polr3a-tamKI cerebella compared to cerebra.
source: However, a comparative DE analysis showed that fewer tRNAs (30 vs 108) and fewer tRNA decoders (11 vs 30) achieved statistical significance in Polr3a-tamKI cerebella compared to cerebra (Figure 6G and H, Supplementary file 6) and the distribution of fold change values spanned a narrower range and was shifted towards smaller differences relative to WT (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative tRNA-seq analysis in Figure 6G and H.

claim: The tRNA profile was minimally altered in cerebella.
source: In addition, the tRNA profile was minimally altered in cerebella (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by tRNA profile analysis in Figure 6—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Bulk RNA-seq data from cerebella showed few significant DE genes (13 genes, p-adj <0.05, log2Fold Change >|0.58|) and limited overlap with cerebral DE genes.
source: These differential effects on the tRNA population in cerebella versus cerebra are consistent with bulk RNA-seq data from cerebella which showed few significant DE genes (13 genes, p-adj <0.05, log2Fold Change >|0.58|, Supplementary file 4) and limited overlap with cerebral DE genes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data in Supplementary file 4 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Any reduction in tRNA decoding potential in cerebella is insufficient to cause significant pathology in this tissue.
source: The minimal effect of the Polr3a mutation on the Pol II transcriptome of cerebella at P42 and the absence of ISR induction at P75 suggests that any reduction in tRNA decoding potential is insufficient to cause significant pathology in this tissue.
evidence: This is an inference based on the minimal transcriptional changes and absence of ISR in cerebella.

claim: The paucity of gross phenotypes identified by histopathology across many Polr3a mutant tissues reflects that cell-specific requirements for a minimum threshold of Pol III transcription have mostly been met.
source: The paucity of gross phenotypes identified by histopathology across many Polr3a mutant tissues reflects that cell-specific requirements for a minimum threshold of Pol III transcription have mostly been met.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limited histopathological findings in most tissues.

claim: tRNA half-lives are either much longer than expected in WT mice and/or that tRNA turnover is decreased in the Polr3a mutant.
source: These changes were paralleled by smaller decreases in mature tRNAs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A) suggesting that tRNA half-lives are either much longer than expected in WT mice (Nwagwu and Nana, 1980) and/or that tRNA turnover is decreased in the Polr3a mutant.
evidence: This is speculation based on the discrepancy between precursor and mature tRNA levels.

claim: The results point to a particularly high sensitivity of cerebra to the Polr3a mutation and a remarkable insensitivity of many non-tRNA transcripts in cerebella, kidney and heart to the reduction in Pol III activity.
source: Given the levels of recombination in these tissues (which were higher in cerebella, kidney, and heart than in cerebra, Figure 3—figure supplement 2C), the results point to a particularly high sensitivity of cerebra to the Polr3a mutation and a remarkable insensitivity of many non-tRNA transcripts in cerebella, kidney and heart to the reduction in Pol III activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparative analysis of multiple tissues.

claim: The insensitivity of non-tRNA transcripts may result from tissue-specific differences in the recruitment of the mutant Pol III to its genes, differences in the stability or nuclease accessibility of the RNA in specific ribonucleoprotein complexes, the ability of some Pol III promoters to be transcribed by RNA polymerase II or other effects that remain to be defined.
source: This insensitivity of non-tRNA transcripts may result from tissue-specific differences in the recruitment of the mutant Pol III to its genes, differences in the stability or nuclease accessibility of the RNA in specific ribonucleoprotein complexes, the ability of some Pol III promoters to be transcribed by RNA polymerase II (Dergai et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2018; James Faresse et al., 2012) or other effects that remain to be defined.
evidence: This is speculation about potential mechanisms supported by citations.

claim: Different thresholds of sensitivity to defects in Pol III transcription exist in different tissues and/or cell populations.
source: Together, these data suggest different thresholds of sensitivity to defects in Pol III transcription in different tissues and/or cell populations.
evidence: This is an inference based on differential responses across tissues.

claim: The more robust activation of microglia in the striatum versus the cortex suggests significant differences in sensitivity to the Polr3a mutation between these regions.
source: Indeed, within the cerebra, the more robust activation of microglia in the striatum versus the cortex suggests significant differences in sensitivity to the Polr3a mutation between these regions.
evidence: This is an inference based on differential microglial activation in different brain regions.

claim: The apparent insensitivity of the cerebella to the Polr3a mutation may reflect that neurogenesis and synapse formation is largely complete by P21, before introduction of the mutation.
source: In contrast to the cerebra, the apparent insensitivity of the cerebella to the Polr3a mutation may reflect that neurogenesis and synapse formation is largely complete by P21, before introduction of the mutation (Zeiss, 2021).
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism underlying cerebellar insensitivity supported by citation.

claim: It remains possible that more subtle phenotypes such as dendritic pruning, which continues in the cerebellum through 2 months of age, may be affected.
source: However, it remains possible that more subtle phenotypes such as dendritic pruning, which continues in the cerebellum through 2 months of age, may be affected (Leto et al., 2016).
evidence: This is speculation about potential undetected phenotypes supported by citation.

claim: Oligodendrocyte lineage cells in the cerebellum have a different threshold for minimal Pol III activity through development and maturation than in other regions of the brain.
source: Together, these observations suggest that oligodendrocyte lineage cells in the cerebellum have a different threshold for minimal Pol III activity through development and maturation than in other regions of the brain.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of cerebellar and cerebral phenotypes in two mouse models.

claim: The sensitivity of the mouse exocrine pancreas to the Polr3a mutation was unexpected given the absence of reports on acinar dysfunction associated with Polr3-related disease.
source: The sensitivity of the mouse exocrine pancreas to the Polr3a mutation was unexpected given the absence of reports on acinar dysfunction associated with Polr3-related disease but is consistent with the knowledge that a Polr3b mutation disrupts development of the exocrine pancreas and intestine in zebrafish (Yee et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim reflects the novelty of the finding and is supported by citation to related work in zebrafish.

claim: The unique codon usage of mouse and human pancreatic acinar cells may underlie the pancreatic phenotype.
source: The unique codon usage of mouse and human pancreatic acinar cells, which differs from most other cell types and is skewed by the codon composition of highly expressed secreted proteins may underlie this phenotype (Gao et al., 2022).
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism supported by citation.

claim: The Polr3a pancreatic phenotype may reflect unique differences in the development of rodent versus human pancreata.
source: Alternatively, the Polr3a pancreatic phenotype may reflect unique differences in the development of rodent versus human pancreata: The increase in the size of mouse pancreas from birth to adulthood results largely from an increase (~19-fold) in the volume of acinar cells (Anzi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is speculation about species-specific differences supported by citation.

claim: Pol III dysfunction and the reduction in the cerebral tRNA population at P42 coincides with behavioral deficits and precedes substantial downstream alterations in the Pol II transcriptome.
source: Pol III dysfunction and the reduction in the cerebral tRNA population at P42 coincides with behavioral deficits and precedes substantial downstream alterations in the Pol II transcriptome, which include induction of an innate immune response (IR) and an ISR, and indicators of neurodegeneration (i.e. activation of cell death pathways and loss of mitochondrial DNA).
evidence: This is an inference based on temporal analysis of molecular and behavioral changes.

claim: Whether the decrease in the abundance of other Pol III transcripts in the cerebrum at later times contributes to disease progression is an open question.
source: Whether the decrease in the abundance of other Pol III transcripts in the cerebrum at later times contributes to disease progression is an open question.
evidence: This acknowledges uncertainty about the role of non-tRNA Pol III transcripts.

claim: These changes in non-tRNA Pol III transcripts may represent secondary effects of IR/ISR signaling or cell death stressors and may be occurring in cells that have already committed to a pathway of programmed cell death.
source: These changes may represent secondary effects of IR/ISR signaling or cell death stressors and may be occurring in cells that have already committed to a pathway of programmed cell death.
evidence: This is speculation about the nature of late-stage changes in Pol III transcripts.

claim: Decreased levels of a single cytoplasmic tRNA isoacceptor or deletion/mutation of a single nuclear-encoded tRNA gene is sufficient to alter translation and cause neuronal dysfunction.
source: Recent studies have shown that decreased levels of a single cytoplasmic tRNA isoacceptor or deletion/mutation of a single nuclear-encoded tRNA gene is sufficient to alter translation and cause neuronal dysfunction: Dominant mutations in the glycyl-tRNA synthetase gene associated with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease CMT2D, cause sequestration of tRNAGly, neuropathy, impair neuronal translation and induce the ISR (Spaulding et al., 2021; Zuko et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Mutation or deletion of the n-TRtct5 isodecoder expressed in neurons reduced the total tRNAArg(UCU) pool, caused ribosome pausing at AGA codons, ISR induction, defects in neuronal function and sensitization to loss of ribosome quality control proteins.
source: Mutation or deletion of the n-TRtct5 isodecoder expressed in neurons, reduced the total tRNAArg(UCU) pool, caused ribosome pausing at AGA codons, ISR induction, defects in neuronal function and sensitization to loss of ribosome quality control proteins (Ishimura et al., 2014; Kapur et al., 2020; Terrey et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Global deletion of the n-TFgaa7 isoacceptor is sufficient to cause transcription and proteomic changes, neurological deficits, increased ribosome stalling, and altered protein expression.
source: Global deletion of the n-TFgaa7 (aka tRNA-Phe-1–1) isoacceptor is sufficient to cause transcription and proteomic changes, neurological deficits, increased ribosome stalling, and altered protein expression (Hughes et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the literature.

claim: The induction of an ATF4-dependent ISR at P42 and its enhancement at P75 is a clear indicator that translation kinetics have been impacted by the global decrease in tRNA abundance.
source: In the cerebra of Polr3a-tamKI mice, the induction of an ATF4-dependent ISR at P42 and its enhancement at P75 is a clear indicator that translation kinetics have been impacted by the global decrease in tRNA abundance, which extends across most decoders and changes the tRNA profile.
evidence: This is an inference based on ISR induction and tRNA changes.

claim: The Polr3a mutation is predicted to compromise translation efficiency and change the frequency and sites of ribosome pausing and/or stalling.
source: Accordingly, the Polr3a mutation is predicted to compromise translation efficiency and change the frequency and sites of ribosome pausing and/or stalling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed tRNA changes and known effects of tRNA availability on translation.

claim: Chronic ISR activation ultimately fails to restore cellular homeostasis, and thus leads to neurodegeneration through amplification of the IR and activation of cell death pathways.
source: We propose that in the context of Polr3-related disease, chronic ISR activation ultimately fails to restore cellular homeostasis, and thus leads to neurodegeneration through amplification of the IR and activation of cell death pathways (Costa-Mattioli and Walter, 2020).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the findings and supported by citation.
